---
title: "Week 2 · Distribution, variance and its applications"
subtitle: "Density and cumulative distributions, variance, quantiles, z-scores and the WHO growth standards"
---

The week moves from describing a variable's centre to describing its whole
distribution. It ends with two applications that come back later in the course:
measuring child stunting against the WHO length-for-age standard, and the
Datasaurus, which shows why a univariate summary is never enough.

## What the deck covers

-   **Distribution**: symmetric and non-symmetric distributions, extreme and
    influential observations; from a density to a cumulative distribution; the
    cumulative distribution of income; applications to income inequality and
    the Lorenz curve, with homework examples.
-   **Variance**: population versus sample variance, the standard deviation,
    and why distributions with the same standard deviation can look very
    different.
-   **Quantiles**: quartiles and deciles for normal and non-normal
    distributions; income deciles; an example on inequality, taxes and
    subsidies; robust versus non-robust measures of spread; matching
    distributions to box plots.
-   **Application of variance in descriptive analysis**: measuring stunting;
    the WHO length/height-for-age standard, how it is built and summarised, and
    following one boy's development against it.
-   **The (standard) normal distribution**: the z-score, why it is needed,
    standardisation, and exam examples on determining stunting status.
-   **When univariate analysis is not enough**: the Datasaurus, a synthetic
    dataset whose univariate summaries hide everything.
-   Reading before Week 4, homework examples on z-scores, variance and the
    normal distribution, a pointer to Our World in Data on income inequality,
    and the key concepts checklist.

## Data used

-   📊 [WHO length/height-for-age standard](../data.qmd#who) (`who_lhfa.rds`).
